answer_text:
We need \(z\) such that

\[
(n+1)z \equiv 1 \pmod{n^2}.
\]

Since

\[
(n+1)(1-n)=1-n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{n^2},
\]

we have

\[
z \equiv 1-n \pmod{n^2}.
\]

As a least positive residue modulo \(n^2\), this is

\[
z = n^2-n+1.
\]

Thus the multiplicative inverse is

\[
\boxed{n^2-n+1}.
\]
